messages:
Sam F.: Heads up 6;#8212; vendor Maple Data Labs submitted invoice MDL-2026-042 and is asking us to gross-up for "US taxes" before payment. Invoice total USD 9,200. They say they won't send a W-8 unless we agree. What do we do?

Priya T.: Are they a corp or an individual? For non-US corps we need W-8BEN-E. For individuals W-8BEN. If services were performed outside the US usually no withholding.

Sam F.: They're a Canadian corporation per vendor record. Contact insists on gross-up because of "possible IRS withholding" if we don't.

CJ M.: Redwood policy: we do not gross-up vendor invoices to cover their tax liabilities unless there's a written contractual obligation. Standard flow: request completed W-8BEN-E and confirmation of service location. Hold payment until we receive form.

Evan L.: I drafted a message to vendor: "Hi Maple Data Labs 6;#8212; thanks for MDL-2026-042. To process payment please provide a completed, signed W-8BEN-E and confirm the country where the services were performed. Per our policy, Redwood will not gross-up invoices for tax liabilities absent a contractual amendment. If services were performed in the US please state so we can route to Tax and Legal. Payment will remain on hold until documentation is received."

Sam F.: OK placing payment on hold and will send that. AP-bot, flag invoice and set a 5-business-day SLA.

AP-bot: Hold placed on MDL-2026-042 6;#8212; reason: missing W-8BEN-E and vendor requested gross-up. Notified AP queue. Hold expiry: 2026-05-09T23:59:00Z.

Priya T.: Note for tax team: if they confirm work was done in Canada and provide W-8BEN-E, no US withholding should apply. If they claim US-sourced services, escalate to Tax for treaty analysis.

CJ M.: Agreed. Do not gross-up. If vendor pushes, escalate to Legal for contract amendment request.

Sam F.: Message sent to vendor at 2026-05-02T18:04:12Z (cc: vendor-ops). Will update thread when they respond. :white_check_mark:
